'''Sam Aronson''' (May 14, 1942 – March 18, 2026<ref>{{cite web |title=Obituary: In remembrance of Samuel Aronson |url=https://tbrnewsmedia.com/obituary-in-remembrance-of-samuel-aronson/ |website=tbrnewsmedia.com |access-date=28 April 2026}}</ref>) was an American physicist.  He served as president of the [[American Physical Society]] in 2015 and was the director of the [[Brookhaven National Laboratory]] from 2006 to 2012.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Samuel Aronson |url=https://history.aip.org/phn/11409016.html |accessdate=January 12, 2016 |publisher=aip.org}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Gewin |first1=Virginia |title=Sam Aronson, director, Brookhaven National Laboratory, Upton, New York |journal=Nature |date=4 October 2006 |volume=443 |issue=7111 |pages=602 |doi=10.1038/nj7111-602a |doi-access=free }}</ref>  

== Biography ==
Aronson was born in [[Huntington, New York]].<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |last=Physics |first=American Institute of |date=2021-09-24 |title=Sam Aronson |url=https://www.aip.org/history-programs/niels-bohr-library/oral-histories/45467 |access-date=2022-07-19 |website=American Institute of Physics |language=en}}</ref> He earned an A.B. in physics from [[Columbia University]] in 1964, and a Ph.D. in physics from [[Princeton University]] in 1968.<ref name=":1" /><ref name=":2">{{Cite web |title=Brookhaven Lab's Sam Aronson Inducted into the Long Island Technology Hall of Fame |url=https://www.bnl.gov/newsroom/news.php?a=111399 |access-date=2022-07-19 |website=Brookhaven National Laboratory |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book |last=Columbia College (Columbia University). Office of Alumni Affairs and Development |url=http://archive.org/details/ldpd_12981092_014 |title=Columbia College today |last2=Columbia College (Columbia University) |date=1966 |publisher=New York, N.Y. : Columbia College, Office of Alumni Affairs and Development |others=Columbia University Libraries}}</ref>

After graduation, Aronson worked at the [[Enrico Fermi Institute for Nuclear Studies]] as a research associate until 1972. He later joined the faculty of the [[University of Wisconsin–Madison]] and was on the faculty until 1977 before joining the accelerator department of the Brookhaven National Laboratory (BNL) as associate physicist. He moved to the Lab's physics department in 1982, became associate chair of the department in 1987, then deputy chair in 1988.<ref name=":2" />

In 1991, Aronson became director of the [[PHENIX detector|PHENIX detector project]], overseeing the construction of the [[Relativistic Heavy Ion Collider]].<ref name=":2" /> He became director of the laboratory’s physics department in 2001. He became associate laboratory director for nuclear and [[particle physics]] in 2005 and was named director in 2006.<ref name=":2" />

In 2013, Aronson became director of the [[Riken|RIKEN]] BNL Research Center.<ref name=":0" /> He served as vice president of the American Physical Society in 2013 and became president in 2015.<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite web |title=Sam Aronson of Brookhaven Elected APS VP |url=http://www.aps.org/publications/apsnews/201208/saronson.cfm |access-date=2022-07-19 |website=www.aps.org |language=en}}</ref>

Aronson was named senior scientist emeritus of the BNL in 2017.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Former Lab Director Samuel Aronson Named Senior Scientist Emeritus |url=https://www.bnl.gov/newsroom/news.php?a=212480 |access-date=2022-07-19 |website=Brookhaven National Laboratory |language=en}}</ref> He is the Secretary of the National Offshore Wind R&D Consortium.<ref>{{Cite web |title=National Offshore Wind R&D Consortium |url=https://www.energy.gov/eere/wind/national-offshore-wind-rd-consortium |access-date=2022-07-19 |website=Energy.gov |language=en}}</ref>

Aronson was a fellow of the [[American Physical Society]] and the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]].<ref name=":2" /><ref>{{Cite web |title=Samuel Aronson Named as AAAS Fellow |url=https://www.bnl.gov/newsroom/news.php?a=110389 |access-date=2022-07-19 |website=Brookhaven National Laboratory |language=en}}</ref>
